# observe_inbound_share_registration_token

Issues a single-use token that proves you own a Snowflake provider account, for registering an `observe_inbound_share`.

-> **Preview:** Inbound shares are in private preview and must be enabled for your tenant. The schema may change.

Set the share comment to `token` (for example with the `comment` argument of `snowflake_share`) before the `observe_inbound_share` is created. The token is stored in Terraform state; treat the state as secret.

The token expires, and issuing a new one retires any earlier token for the same provider account. To get a new token, replace this resource with `terraform apply -replace`. Destroying this resource only removes it from state.
## Example Usage
```terraform
resource "observe_inbound_share_registration_token" "acme" {
  provider_account = "ACME_CORP.PROD"
}

# Prove ownership by setting the share comment to the token
resource "snowflake_share" "customer_data" {
  name     = "CUSTOMER_SHARE_PROD"
  comment  = observe_inbound_share_registration_token.acme.token
  accounts = [data.observe_inbound_share_setup.setup.consumer_account]
}

data "observe_inbound_share_setup" "setup" {}
```
<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `provider_account` (String) Org-qualified Snowflake account that provides the share, as `<ORG>.<ACCOUNT>`. Changing this issues a new token.

### Read-Only

- `expires_at` (String) When the token expires. Register the share before then.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `setup_sql` (List of Object, Sensitive) SQL that sets the share comment to the token, for when the share is not managed by Terraform. Replace `<your_share_name>` with the share's name and run it in the provider account. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--setup_sql))
- `token` (String, Sensitive) The registration token. Set it as the share comment, exactly as returned.

### Nested Schema for `setup_sql`

Read-Only:

- `description` (String)
